D1 research authoring, batch 81 (2026-09-27): two ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1 and 2 (bulimia-nervosa, anxiety-disorder) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. Both edges share the same three anchors because the largest located comparative study reports eating-disorder and psychiatric-disorder history as components of a single case-control model rather than as separable findings.

Classification guard: both edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) at PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL. Both causation statuses record openly that the largest anchor modelled psychiatric and eating-disorder history as a RISK FACTOR FOR rumination syndrome at adjusted odds ratios of 16.4 and 4.47 rather than modelling rumination syndrome as the exposure, so the direction of the relationship is unresolved and neither edge may be presented as either condition producing the other. A substantial component of both overlaps is recorded as plausibly diagnostic rather than causal, because rumination syndrome is classified within the feeding and eating disorders and a prior eating-disorder label may reflect reclassification rather than a preceding illness.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no depressive-disorder edge (DUPLICATE-SCOPE - the registry already carries bulimia-nervosa to depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder to depressive-disorder, so a third direct route would duplicate a relationship the graph already resolves through two registered chains, and authoring it would add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict to the standing CRG review set); no dental-abrasion-erosion-abfraction or dental-erosion edge (MECHANISM-UNSUPPORTED - rumination syndrome regurgitates undigested food without the acid exposure that drives erosive tooth wear in bulimia nervosa, and all located dental-erosion evidence in this space is drawn from eating-disorder populations rather than rumination syndrome cohorts); no gastroparesis edge (already registered as diabetic-gastroparesis to gastroparesis, and the located rumination-syndrome cohorts exclude delayed gastric emptying as the differential rather than reporting it as a consequence); and the identity distinction recorded in the governance note, namely that the catalog rumination-syndrome is the gastrointestinal rumination disorder and is a different entity from cognitive rumination in depression, so no edge in this file may be justified by the psychological construct.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rumination syndrome and bulimia nervosa co-occur at a rate far above matched controls, and the single largest comparative study designs the finding as a case-control contrast rather than a coincidence of presentation: a tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 adults with rumination syndrome against 48 age- and gender-matched controls reports a history of eating disorder in 37.5 percent of rumination syndrome patients against 4.2 percent of controls (Fisher exact p=0.0002), with anorexia nervosa at 16.7 percent against 0 percent (p=0.005) and bulimia nervosa at 21.1 percent against 0 percent (p=0.001), and with eating-disorder history surviving multivariable adjustment as an independent predictor of rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 (p=0.0033) (PMID 33988353); an adolescent case series of eight referred girls reports six diagnosed with rumination syndrome, most of whom carried a co-occurring anxiety, depressive, or eating-disorder diagnosis including anorexia and bulimia (PMID 42217214); and a bidirectional 101-patient paediatric cohort separating early-childhood-onset from adolescent-onset rumination syndrome reports the adolescent-onset phenotype as the one carrying the eating-disorder and mood comorbidity, with 23 percent depression and 40 percent anxiety confined to the adolescent-onset group against 0 percent and 14 percent in the early-onset group, and with the authors concluding explicitly that the pathogenesis and natural history of the two onset strata may be distinct (PMID 38504395); recorded as documented association only, and with the direction of the relationship carried as unresolved because the largest anchor's own model treats eating-disorder history as a RISK FACTOR FOR rumination syndrome rather than the reverse, so the edge is registered as a bidirectional co-occurrence requiring separate documentation of each diagnosis rather than as a claim that either produces the other.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established in either direction, and the located anchor argues actively against fixing a direction: the largest comparative study modelled prior eating-disorder history as a risk factor for rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 rather than modelling rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a later eating-disorder diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is asserted by that design rather than demonstrated by it; a substantial share of the apparent overlap is plausibly diagnostic rather than causal, because rumination syndrome is classified within the feeding and eating disorders in current diagnostic nomenclature and a prior eating-disorder label may reflect reclassification of the same undifferentiated regurgitation behaviour rather than a distinct illness preceding it; the two entities also differ in mechanism, since rumination syndrome is an effortless postprandial retrograde flow of undigested contents driven by an automatic autonomic reflex, whereas bulimia nervosa is a deliberate binge-and-purge behaviour, so shared abdominal distress, dietary restriction, and body-image disturbance can produce convergent presentations without either driving the other; and the adolescent anchors are a case series and a single-centre bidirectional cohort, neither of which includes a rumination-syndrome-free comparison group for the eating-disorder outcome. Individual claims require a dated, separately signed diagnosis of bulimia nervosa with documented binge and purge episodes, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis documenting effortless regurgitation of undigested food, the chronology of which diagnosis came first, and explicit clinician exclusion of vomiting as a learned behaviour or of regurgitation as a learned behaviour before the two are recorded as co-occurring.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared gut-brain behavioural circuit rather than a lesion: repeated postprandial regurgitation, abdominal discomfort, early satiety, and fear of feeding produce food avoidance, meal skipping, and weight loss in rumination syndrome, and a pre-existing eating-disorder framework supplies body-image disturbance and a restrictive behavioural repertoire, with either state able to maintain the other through the well-described feedback loop in which restriction worsens postprandial discomfort and in which regurgitation relieves the discomfort of eating; the loop is named as the plausible common pathway because the located cohorts report the comorbidity without experimentally separating the direction, and whether one condition recruits or maintains the other in any given patient remains hypothesized until the chronology of onset is documented.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at matched case-control, adolescent case-series, and bidirectional paediatric-cohort class following the file's own gastrointestinal and behavioural framing and the registry's treatment- and behaviour-mediated precedent classes: the case-control anchor is the only located design with a matched comparison group and is the anchor that supplies the effect sizes, the significance thresholds, and the independent-adjusted odds ratio, and it is registered together with its own directional framing (PMID 33988353); the adolescent case series supplies the contemporary paediatric observation and the explicit caution that diagnosis is frequently delayed because the presentation is mistaken for reflux or vomiting (PMID 42217214); the bidirectional cohort is registered as the anchor that bounds the claim by showing the comorbidity is concentrated in the adolescent-onset stratum and absent in the early-onset stratum, which is direct evidence against a single uniform mechanism across all rumination syndrome (PMID 38504395). Because the largest anchor models the relationship in the opposite direction to the edge's name, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, records the direction as unresolved in the causation status, and routes individual attribution through dated, separately signed diagnoses of each condition plus clinician exclusion of learned vomiting or learned regurgitation.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational and none establishes temporal order; the largest anchor is a single-tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 cases, so its adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 rests on few exposed individuals and is vulnerable to wide confidence intervals that the abstract does not report; the direction of the model is reversed relative to the edge, so it cannot be cited as evidence that rumination syndrome produces a later eating-disorder diagnosis; the adolescent case series has no comparison group and reports six of eight referred patients, a referral-enriched sample; the bidirectional cohort reports mood comorbidity percentages but not eating-disorder prevalence stratified by onset group, so the claim that the eating-disorder overlap is concentrated in adolescent-onset disease is carried from the depression and anxiety figures rather than from a reported eating-disorder comparison; no located anchor measures regurgitant characteristics such as acidity or enamel exposure, so the rumination-syndrome-to-dental-erosion route was reviewed and withheld as MECHANISM-UNSUPPORTED, because undigested regurgitation is qualitatively different from the acid-laden self-induced vomiting of bulimia nervosa, and the published dental-erosion evidence in this space is drawn from eating-disorder populations rather than from rumination syndrome cohorts.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Bulimia nervosa or binge-eating disorder as a pre-existing, independently diagnosed condition whose behavioural effects may drive food avoidance and regurgitation
Diagnosed vomiting as a learned or intentional behaviour, which would reclassify the presentation away from rumination syndrome entirely
Gastroesophageal reflux disease, achalasia, and delayed gastric emptying, which were excluded in the located cohorts by normal gastric emptying studies but must be excluded individually
Organic CNS disease, in which one adolescent case in the located series was found to have an underlying organic medical illness

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because it is the strongest quantified co-occurrence in the located evidence for this file, because the target identity has zero registered incoming edges, and because the edge is operationally useful in a benefits context where a veteran whose regurgitation is documented as rumination syndrome may also carry a separately diagnosed eating disorder that the regurgitation label conceals. The conservative framing records the direction of the relationship as unresolved and notes openly that the largest anchor models the association in the reverse direction, names the shared gut-brain feedback loop as a hypothesized rather than demonstrated mechanism, bounds the claim with the onset-stratum finding showing the comorbidity is not uniform across rumination syndrome, and requires dated separate diagnoses plus exclusion of learned behaviour before any individual attribution.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Anxiety is the most consistently reported psychiatric correlate of rumination syndrome across three independent designs that span adult, adolescent, and paediatric populations, and the largest of them reports the association surviving multivariable adjustment: a tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 adults with rumination syndrome against 48 matched controls reports 83.3 percent of rumination syndrome patients carrying a psychiatric disorder against 50.0 percent of controls (p=0.0062), with anxiety present in 37.5 percent and depression in 29.2 percent, and with psychiatric-disorder history remaining an independent adjusted predictor of rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 4.47 (p=0.029) (PMID 33988353); an adolescent case series reports that most of the six adolescents diagnosed with rumination syndrome carried co-occurring emotional or psychiatric difficulty, explicitly naming anxiety alongside depression and eating disorders, and identifies delayed diagnosis resulting from the presentation being mistaken for reflux or vomiting (PMID 42217214); and a bidirectional 101-patient paediatric cohort reports anxiety in 40 percent of adolescent-onset disease against 14 percent of early-childhood-onset disease (p=0.004), the same stratum that carries 23 percent depression and the one the authors identify as potentially distinct in pathogenesis (PMID 38504395); recorded as documented association only, with the same reversed modelling direction carried openly, since the largest anchor again treats psychiatric history as a risk factor for rumination syndrome rather than the converse.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety is established for any individual, and the direction is unresolved for the same reasons that apply to the file's eating-disorder edge: the largest comparative anchor modelled psychiatric-disorder history as a risk factor FOR rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 4.47, not rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a subsequent anxiety diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is a design choice rather than a finding; a substantial component of the overlap is plausibly reactive rather than causal, because a chronic, visible, embarrassing, and socially stigmatising regurgitation behaviour with associated weight loss and meal avoidance is an obvious precipitant of anxiety and of social avoidance, and the located series documents embarrassment and distress as central features without establishing whether any anxiety preceded them; the two conditions also share a documented transdiagnostic mechanism in which repetitive negative thinking and emotion-regulation difficulty appear in both, which permits either condition to recruit the other; and no located anchor measures anxiety before the onset of regurgitation. Individual claims require a dated anxiety diagnosis with documented symptom history predating or postdating regurgitation onset, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis, and clinician separation of situational anxiety about the illness from a pre-existing anxiety disorder.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared emotion-regulation circuit operating through the gut-brain axis together with a reactive distress pathway: repetitive negative thinking about eating and the body, avoidance of public eating, and rumination in the cognitive sense are all documented transdiagnostic features that maintain each other, while the physical experience of effortless regurgitation, meal avoidance, and visible weight loss supplies an independent and sufficient reason for anxiety to develop; the pathway is named as a two-part mechanism because the located evidence supports the reactive route as the more readily documented and the shared-circuit route as the more speculative, and which route predominates in any given patient remains hypothesized until the anxiety chronology is established relative to regurgitation onset.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at matched case-control, adolescent case-series, and bidirectional paediatric-cohort class alongside the file's rank 1 eating-disorder edge, which shares the same three anchors because the largest comparative study reports both as components of a single 83.3 percent psychiatric-disorder figure rather than as separable findings: the case-control anchor supplies the only comparison group and the only adjusted estimate (PMID 33988353); the case series supplies the adolescent observation and the documented diagnostic-delay mechanism (PMID 42217214); and the bidirectional cohort supplies the onset-stratum bound showing anxiety is concentrated in adolescent-onset disease and is comparatively uncommon in early-childhood-onset disease (PMID 38504395). Because the largest anchor's direction is reversed relative to the edge and because the reactive pathway is at least as plausible as the shared-circuit pathway, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, records direction as unresolved, and routes individual attribution through dated diagnoses on both sides with explicit separation of situational from pre-existing anxiety.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational and none establishes temporal order; the case-control anchor reports 83.3 percent psychiatric-disorder prevalence against 50.0 percent in controls, but the 50 percent control figure is itself high and indicates that the comparison group was not a healthy population, which narrows the interpretable effect; the psychiatric-disorder exposure in that study is a composite and the anxiety-specific contribution is reported as 37.5 percent of cases without a matching control percentage, so the anxiety-specific risk difference cannot be reconstructed from the abstract; the adolescent case series is a referral-enriched series of eight referred patients with no comparison group; the bidirectional cohort reports anxiety by onset stratum but not by severity, treatment, or duration, and its adolescent-onset group is overwhelmingly female, so sex composition is an uncontrolled confounder; no located anchor uses a structured anxiety instrument reported in the abstract, and no anchor separates pre-existing from reactive anxiety, which is the single most important unresolved question for this edge. The file's depressive-disorder route was reviewed and withheld as DUPLICATE-SCOPE rather than authored, because the registry already carries bulimia-nervosa to depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder to depressive-disorder, so a third direct rumination-syndrome to depressive-disorder edge would duplicate a relationship the graph already resolves through two registered chains.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing anxiety disorder predating the onset of regurgitation, which would reverse the presumed reactive direction
Situtional or illness-related anxiety about regurgitation in public, which is a consequence rather than a co-occurring disorder
Gastroesophageal reflux disease, functional dyspepsia, and other organic gastrointestinal causes of regurgitation
Developmental delay and neurodevelopmental comorbidity, reported at 24 percent in the early-childhood-onset stratum of the located cohort

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because anxiety is the most consistently reported psychiatric correlate of rumination syndrome across all three located designs, because the target identity is a clinically load-bearing one whose presence materially changes management of a regurgitation presentation, and because the located onset-stratum finding shows the association is concentrated in adolescent and adult disease rather than being uniform. The conservative framing records the reversed modelling direction of the largest anchor, distinguishes reactive from pre-existing anxiety as the pivotal unresolved question, names the shared transdiagnostic circuit as hypothesized, and withholds the parallel depressive-disorder route as duplicate-scope against two already-registered chains.
